title: Progressive recovery notice and customer action guide - Dec 2026
content:
Context and purpose:

This doc is a customer-facing draft combining: (A) a short status page update we will publish during progressive recovery, and (B) a concise post-incident summary and action guide for affected customers. Use this when we have partial service restoration but some customers still observe elevated latency or higher error rates on specific routes. The goal is: clear expectations, recommended customer actions (temporary workarounds), and a short timeline for follow-ups.

Summary for customers (2–3 lines):
On 2026-12-27 at ~21:10 UTC Redwood experienced an internal routing regression that increased latency and triggered intermittent 5xx errors for generation endpoints in eu-west-1. Majority of capacity recovered via an automated rollback by 22:05 UTC; residual elevated tail latency persisted for some routes until 23:45 UTC. No raw customer data was exposed. We are providing this recovery update and a brief action guide.

Impact (customer-facing):
- Affected services: text-generation, chat-streaming, model inference routes pinned to small-capacity backends in eu-west-1.
- Symptom: increased 95th/99th percentile latency and occasional 5xx errors (rate ~0.4% peak for affected routes).
- Window: 2026-12-27 21:10 UTC to 2026-12-27 23:45 UTC (majority recovered 22:05 UTC).
- Customer-visible consequences: slower responses, some streaming sessions reset, retry storms observed in a subset of customer SDK versions that aggressively retried.

Immediate actions we took (overview):
1) Triggered automated rollback to last-known-good routing policy at 21:53 UTC (reduced error rate quickly).
2) Scaled additional dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 to absorb persistent tail latency starting 22:10 UTC.
3) Throttled a small percentage of background batch jobs that were contending for GPU I/O at 22:25 UTC.
4) Deployed a hotfix to the routing checker to improve health evaluation thresholds at 23:10 UTC.

Customer action guide (recommended, optional):
- If you observed repeated 5xx errors during this window: retry requests with exponential backoff (base 250ms) and cap retries to 3. Avoid tight synchronous retry loops.
- If you use SDK v0.9.x: upgrade to v0.9.4 which includes better client-side jitter for backoff. (link to release notes in linked artifacts).
- For customers on private/dedicated deployments: confirm your routing policy allows region fallbacks (if you prefer cross-region fallback we can enable for you temporarily via support ticket).
- If you rely on streaming: consider enabling the streaming-fallback toggle which will return chunked payloads sooner at slightly reduced throughput (contact support to toggle).

Suggested status page phrasing (short update we will publish now):
Title: Partial service disruption in eu-west-1 — majority resolved\nUpdate: We experienced a service routing regression affecting generation endpoints in eu-west-1 starting 21:10 UTC. An automated rollback and targeted capacity scale reduced errors; most customers returned to normal by 22:05 UTC. A small set of routes saw elevated tail latency until 23:45 UTC. We continue to monitor and will publish a short post-incident summary within 48 hours.

Follow-up postmortem summary (customer-oriented, to publish within 48 hours):
- Root cause (short): A mis-evaluated routing health check combined with a low-capacity scheduling decision caused a subset of requests to be routed to overloaded backends.
- Contributing factors: aggressive health eviction thresholds, simultaneous background batch traffic, and an SDK retry pattern that amplified transient failures.
- Why customer-visible: the routing decision increased queueing at some GPU workers leading to higher tail latency and intermittent 5xx responses for requests that could not be serviced within configured timeouts.
- Data exposure: none detected. Logs and traces indicate no unauthorized data access.
- Mitigations completed: automated rollback, capacity scale, health-check threshold fix, and targeted throttling of background jobs.
- Planned long-term actions (owner + ETA):
  * Owner: eng-serving-runtime, ETA: 2027-01-14 — revisit and broaden health-check evaluation window and add hysteresis to prevent cascade evictions.
  * Owner: platform-engineering, ETA: 2027-01-07 — introduce a soft-shed policy for background batch jobs during regional stress.
  * Owner: developer-experience, ETA: 2027-01-05 — publish SDK best-practice guide for retries and backoff; release v0.10.0 with improved jitter defaults.
  * Owner: observability, ETA: 2027-01-10 — add a customer-visible signal on status page that identifies impacted routes and a per-route ETA for recovery.

Customer compensation / credits (if applicable):
We review SLA impact after the internal postmortem. If your account meets the SLA criteria for a partial outage during the incident window, our CS team will reach out with a proposed credit and reconciliation steps within 10 business days.

How to contact us:
- If you need immediate assistance, open a support ticket and reference: INCIDENT-2026-12-27-EU-RG. Use priority: "incident-customer" if production traffic is impacted.
- For dedicated/private customers who want a temporary routing change or increased capacity, request an "ops-exception" via your account manager.

Draft email / message template for targeted customers (short):
Subject: Update — Partial service disruption in eu-west-1 resolved (Dec 27)\Body:
Hi <CustomerName>,
We wanted to let you know we experienced a routing regression on Dec 27 that caused elevated latency for some requests in eu-west-1. Most customers recovered by 22:05 UTC and the remaining routes returned to baseline by 23:45 UTC. No data exposure detected. If you saw degraded performance and would like help assessing retries or toggles, reply to this email or open a support ticket and we’ll prioritize.
Thanks,
Asha (Customer Success) on behalf of the Ops & Eng teams

Notes for internal CS/SE reviewers (quick checklist before posting):
- Confirm linked artifacts (JIRA, Confluence, Slack) are included in the public postmortem.
- Coordinate with product/observability to provide per-route metrics for affected customers.
- Decide compensation eligibility cadence and notify legal if any enterprise customers request expedited credits.
- Mark the status page update as "partial-recovery" and schedule the full postmortem publish 48 hours after incident close.

Open questions / items to resolve before finalizing (internal):
1) Do we surface list of impacted routes by customer? (privacy/ops decision)
2) Final wording around credits (legal signoff required for enterprise accounts).
3) Confirm exact SDK versions impacted and finalize rollout notes.

Appendix: brief timeline (internal timeline for accuracy)
- 2026-12-27 21:08 UTC — anomaly detectors report elevated tail latency in eu-west-1.
- 2026-12-27 21:10 UTC — customer-visible 5xx errors begin; incident declared.
- 2026-12-27 21:28 UTC — engineering escalated; initial hypothesis: routing/health eviction.
- 2026-12-27 21:53 UTC — automated rollback initiated to previous routing policy.
- 2026-12-27 22:05 UTC — majority of customers return to nominal behavior.
- 2026-12-27 22:10 UTC — additional capacity scaled; background jobs throttled.
- 2026-12-27 23:10 UTC — routing health-check threshold hotfix deployed.
- 2026-12-27 23:45 UTC — residual elevated tail latency resolved; incident moved to "monitoring".

End of draft. Please review for tone (concise, blame-minimizing) and accuracy before publishing to the status page or sending targeted customer emails.
